MCD.rationale: MCD is a structurally excellent franchise — 95% franchised, 45% operating margins, 22% global QSR share — but the near-term trajectory is mixed. YoY growth is positive (revenue +9.4%, EPS +6.9%) and the stock has de-rated ~21% from highs to ~24x annualized P/E, near the low end of its historical 22-28x corridor. However, QoQ earnings deceleration is material (EPS -12.6%, OCF -29.6%), net margin is drifting lower (32.2% → 31.6%), and management has signaled 'meaningful deceleration' in Q2 comparable sales. The consumer backdrop is challenged with lower-income traffic declining and April comps slightly negative. Value-menu initiatives (McValue platform) risk further margin compression. The crude oil decline (WTI -22.4%) is a genuine input-cost tailwind, and rising rates (10y at 4.68%, Baa at 6.32%) pressure the leveraged balance sheet. The Q2 earnings report on August 4 is a near-term catalyst but the direction of the print is uncertain given management's own deceleration warning. Net: a world-class franchise at a reasonable but not compelling valuation, navigating a difficult cyclical moment with limited visibility on earnings stabilization. Mildly positive on balance — the quality and de-rating provide a floor, but the trajectory and catalysts are not strong enough to warrant a higher conviction score.
key_factors: YoY revenue +9.4% and EPS +6.9% confirm business is growing, not contracting (Q1 2026)
Operating margin 45.2% and net margin 30.4% remain world-class; franchise-heavy model at 95% franchised
Stock at ~24x annualized P/E (close $268.44) sits at low end of historical 22-28x corridor after -21% decline from 52-week high of $341.75
QoQ EPS decline -12.6% and OCF decline -29.6% signal earnings deceleration beyond seasonal norms
Net margin erosion from 32.2% (Sep 2025) to 31.6% (Jul 2026) — directionally negative
Management signaled 'meaningful deceleration' in Q2 2026 comparable sales from Q1's 3.9% pace; April comps slightly negative in U.S. and International Operated Markets
Lower-income consumer traffic continues to decline; value-menu push (McValue platform) with 50/50 cost-sharing with franchisees risks margin compression
WTI crude declined -22.4% to $85.15 — material tailwind for food and energy input costs
Rising rates (10y 4.68%, Baa 6.32%) increase cost of capital on leveraged balance sheet with negative equity of -$1.29B
Q2 2026 earnings report on August 4, 2026 is a near-term catalyst; consensus expects revenue ~$7.16B and EPS ~$3.34
49 consecutive years of dividend increases — one year from Dividend King status; disciplined capital returns
Digital channels at ~40% of top-market systemwide sales in Q1 2026, up from ~35% YoY; 166M loyalty members
